description: Learners revisit algebraic expressions from earlier grades and meet the special expressions called linear polynomials through everyday contexts such as counting pens and pencils in sealed boxes.
Learners identify a linear polynomial as an expression in which the variable appears to the first power, using examples such as the perimeter 4x of a square and a club fee of 200 + 50x rupees.
Learners study a growing pattern of square tiles, tabulate the number of tiles at each stage, and write a linear rule that predicts the count at any stage of the pattern.
Learners use linear expressions to model situations that grow or decline at a constant rate, such as a journey cost C(d) = 100 + 60d, and read the growth or decay from a table of values.
Learners express the relationship between two variables in the form y = ax + b, and determine the values of a and b from given pairs of values such as data usage and a monthly bill.
Learners plot a linear equation y = ax + b as a straight line by identifying two points on it, and read the equation of a line back from the coordinates of points lying on it.
